title: November 24 — from shared memory to semantic grain
summary: Ten projects connect graph memory, active identification, Walsh geometry and frozen-model semantic grain. The original category gain is not yet established across frames. Sihti core/residue is an explicit conceptual ancestor, not a shared mechanism.

nodes.claim: Tests positive, signed, binary and phase edge memory against ordinary slots.
nodes.survived: Prior audit signed B MSE 0.018213 vs phase 0.024474; slot baselines and real/sham rewrite probes are explicit.
nodes.killed: No general distributed-memory benefit established; read FLOPs not matched.
nodes.era: November 24: protected memory, semantic grain and discriminating probes

nodes.claim: Extends graph memory to K=2,4,8 and separates writer from reader limitations.
nodes.survived: CPU pilot: slots win every K; at K=4 slots 0.0152 chain MSE vs signed 0.0413 and raw-byte direct 0.0416.
nodes.killed: Elastic pressure sweep fails. Single-seed pilot, not full GPU gate; raw-byte control is not proof against all possible readers.
nodes.era: November 24: protected memory, semantic grain and discriminating probes

nodes.claim: Selects equal-energy probes to distinguish competing models and abstain on equivalent hypotheses.
nodes.survived: Adaptive pair separation and Bayesian EIG each correctly identify 139/144 groups with zero confidently wrong and five abstentions.
nodes.killed: Ties standard EIG; known model library; real benchmark runs unexecuted.
nodes.era: November 24: protected memory, semantic grain and discriminating probes

nodes.claim: Interactive wire-price, rank-cut, curvature, crossing and MERA min-cut illustrations.
nodes.survived: Python and JS checks agree for small crossing tables q=2,3,4.
nodes.killed: Explains AI-authored VP versus VNP proof claim; does not verify proof, resolve P vs NP or measure physical prices.
nodes.era: November 24: protected memory, semantic grain and discriminating probes

nodes.claim: Walsh chessboards, state-dependent XOR read/write and Soar multiscale search.
nodes.survived: Thresholded search finds three injected patterns 200/200; flying without writing beats fixed and random search in toy.
nodes.killed: Each bucket touches whole vector; not faster than fast Walsh here. Fixed wire beats moving read in one-way world; repository reader not yet verified.
nodes.era: November 24: protected memory, semantic grain and discriminating probes

nodes.claim: Numeric activation coarsening tests native/rotated/J-subspace directions, matched energy and restoration.
nodes.survived: V2 adds whole-suffix cuts, aligned donor checks and nonlexical fine properties after V1 audit.
nodes.killed: No validated semantic-grain result in README; fake quantization is not a storage or speedup claim.
nodes.era: November 24: protected memory, semantic grain and discriminating probes

nodes.claim: Frozen Qwen3-1.7B sibling-mean clamp through block 12 tests kind versus identity.
nodes.survived: 22/22 held-out leaves gain category evidence (+3.92 nats); identity drops 22/22 to 3/22. Category-word move −0.58; random −6.61. Open label 7/8 from means vs fixed first exemplar 2/8.
nodes.killed: Random matched category-word length, not sibling length. Eight supplied families, one checkpoint. Sign residue restores 18/22, below preregistered 80% recovery. Theory weakens amplification.
nodes.era: November 24: protected memory, semantic grain and discriminating probes

nodes.claim: Live common thread, odd-one-out, blends, caricature and activation arithmetic.
nodes.survived: Implements neutral-slot clamp, calibrated readouts and open-ended descriptions.
nodes.killed: Not independent replication; multi-token and prompt dependence; no universal concept algebra.
nodes.era: November 24: protected memory, semantic grain and discriminating probes

nodes.claim: Combines letter constraints, calibrated clue scores and optional second-meaning activation average.
nodes.survived: Pattern filters proposals; early-layer patch ranks candidates by both meanings.
nodes.killed: Can miss answers; no held-out crossword benchmark or superiority established.
nodes.era: November 24: protected memory, semantic grain and discriminating probes

nodes.claim: Shared/private semantic geometry, emerging taxonomy, state repair, adaptive walks and independent cue evidence.
nodes.survived: Chat prototype gain 46/46, synthetic siblings tie real; Pythia external map precedes native answers. Head 003 corrected cue intersection 17/144 vs native 7/144 and union 2/144; both gates pass.
nodes.killed: Special sibling synergy and normalization explanation unsupported. Iris routing, Bridge PCA writeback, Ocular band selection and Head 001/002 performance gates fail. Head 003 has unequal prompts, vocabulary and compute; 11.8% absolute accuracy.
nodes.era: November 24: protected memory, semantic grain and discriminating probes

edges.why: Original writer, decoder and protocol retained.
Extends transport code to K items.
Extends identifiability question into active probe instrument.
Cuts and spectral patterns motivate separate Walsh toy.
Sister numeric and semantic grain experiments.
Adapts activation averaging to two-meaning ranking.
Repairs random matching and tests synthetic siblings.

motifs.title: What can shared representation forget, and what must remain owned?
motifs.description: Graph memory exposes interference; sibling averaging preserves kind while erasing names; Theory tests whether shared means suffice. Conceptual convergence, not a universal mechanism.

motifs.title: Probe choice and strong baselines delimit identification
motifs.description: Matched controls constrain memory, known-library and semantic claims.
